title: Let each terminal have one transaction in flight

blocks.text: A parking-garage network allows one transaction in flight per terminal. Its terminals give up after 20 seconds and send the next request at once, and the network wants that request declined while the first one is still being processed. The switch runs two TransactionManagers, one for purchases and one for refunds, and each has its own instance of the participant that uses `TerminalLock`.
Finish `claim` and `release` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/TerminalLock.java`. The claims live in the space the class is given, under `key(terminal)`. When you're done:

items: a terminal with a transaction in flight is refused, whichever TransactionManager asks, even when both ask at the same moment;
a session that hangs and never calls `release` does not lock its terminal for longer than `maxHold` milliseconds;
after `release` the terminal's next request is accepted at once.

blocks.text: About four lines in total. The tests use a space that records how each entry was written, and in one test it makes two callers meet in the middle of their work.

cases.says: a claimed terminal refuses a second claim, and other terminals are unaffected
a claim nobody takes carries a lease, so a hung or dead session does not lock the terminal for good
the check and the write happen under the space's lock, so two instances claiming at once get one claim
releasing takes the entry away; writing a 'free' value over it leaves the key occupied

origin.section: 12.3 The Space's Own Operations Are Atomic, and a Read Followed by a Write Is Not

concepts: An entry nobody takes stays until it is taken, so marks and claims carry a lease.
Each Space operation is atomic but a read followed by a write is not; the two steps go under the space's lock, with outIfEmpty, nextLong or synchronized on the space.
